short: An airborne corridor into the Netherlands that stopped one bridge short of the Rhine.
full:
Montgomery proposed to cross the Rhine at Arnhem and turn the northern end of the West Wall, with the aim of ending the war in 1944. Three and a half airborne divisions were to seize a sixty-mile corridor of bridges from Eindhoven to Arnhem on 17 September, and XXX Corps would drive up a single road to relieve them. The American divisions took most of their objectives, though the Nijmegen bridge held out until a costly assault crossing of the Waal on the 20th.

The British 1st Airborne landed six to eight miles from the Arnhem bridge, with radios that largely failed, in a sector where two refitting SS panzer divisions happened to be resting. A single battalion under Frost held the northern ramp of the bridge for four days. The relief column never arrived. Of about 10,600 men landed north of the Rhine, some 1,500 were killed and 6,400 taken prisoner. The Netherlands north of the rivers stayed occupied through a winter famine that killed around 20,000 Dutch civilians.
